title: [rereview] project-LICHEN-da2q.16.3: Duplicate lichen_tdma_compute_slot in link_ctx.c and tdma.c with CONCAT vs XOR (linker symbol conflict)
description:
**Severity: P1 (build break / correctness bug)**

The commit claims to have removed the duplicate , but it is still defined in TWO files with TWO different algorithms:

1. **link_ctx.c:666** — CONCAT approach: hashes 12-byte buffer (eui64[0..8] ++ epoch[0..4] LE). This matches the test vectors () and the  function in Python.

2. **tdma.c:20** (guarded by ) — XOR approach: XORs each byte of eui64 with one byte of epoch (repeating due to shift), then hashes only 8 bytes. This does NOT match the test vectors.

Both files also define duplicate , , and  with the same signatures — guaranteeing a linker error when CONFIG_LICHEN_TDMA is enabled.

When epoch=0, both implementations produce identical results (XOR with zero is identity, concat with LE-zero bytes doesn't change hash). For any epoch>0, they diverge. No existing test catches this because all test vectors use epoch=0.

**Fix:** The functions in  (the CONCAT version) match the spec and test vectors. The duplicate in  must be removed (or guarded so it's not compiled when link_ctx.c provides them). The  versions use  but the TDMA functions lack that guard.

**Related:** Python  uses XOR-into-first-4-bytes (different from tdma.c XOR-all-8), while  uses CONCAT. Python has an internal inconsistency too.

**Files:** link_ctx.c, tdma.c, python/src/lichen/sim/tdma.py, CMakeLists.txt
